blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team keeps three copies of its depot-siting builder, one each for HiGHS, SCIP and CP-SAT, and they keep drifting apart. Rewritten in MathOpt, what differs between a HiGHS run and a SCIP run?

options.text: Only the SolverType given to mathopt.solve, since the model names no solver
options.says: Right: the model is solver-independent; the lesson ran one built model on five solvers by changing that argument.

options.text: The variables' types, since SCIP needs integer variables of its own kind
options.says: A MathOpt variable is the same for every solver: bounds and an integer flag.

options.text: The import line, since each solver has its own MathOpt module to build with
options.says: Every program imports one module, ortools.math_opt.python.mathopt, whatever the solver.

options.text: The Model call, since the solver must be named when the model is created
options.says: mathopt.Model takes a name only; the solver is named at solve time.

origin.section: The Solver Is an Argument to solve, Never Part of the Model

questions.stem: A maximization with continuous tonnage variables and integer truck counts is solved twice: CP-SAT reports OPTIMAL 1,840 and HiGHS reports OPTIMAL 1,905. Which value is the optimum of the model as written?

options.text: 1,840, since CP-SAT's OPTIMAL proves no plan of the model does better
options.says: CP-SAT answered a model with the tonnage rounded to whole numbers; its OPTIMAL is about that model, as the lesson's 22,532 against 23,669.5 shows.

options.text: 1,905, since CP-SAT rounded the continuous values to whole numbers
options.says: Right: CP-SAT discretizes continuous variables and still reports OPTIMAL; HiGHS solves the model as written.

options.text: Either, since two OPTIMAL values differ only within the solvers' tolerances
options.says: A tolerance moves a value by a tiny fraction; 1,840 against 1,905 is a different model, as in the lesson's CP-SAT run.

options.text: Neither, since a model with continuous variables has no optimum in a MIP solver
options.says: HiGHS solves models with continuous and integer variables to proven optimality, as the lesson's one-continuous model shows.

origin.section: CP-SAT Needs Integers, and Rounds a Continuous Model Without Warning

questions.stem: An analyst solves a regional LP with SCIP, gets OPTIMAL, and then calls `result.dual_values(budget_2028)` for finance. What happens?

options.text: It returns the row's price, since SCIP solves the LP with simplex as GLOP does
options.says: The lesson's SCIP run of the LP relaxation returned no dual solution, whatever method it used.

options.text: It returns 0.0 for the row, since SCIP prices only the rows of a MILP
options.says: There is no price to return: no solver gives MILP duals, and SCIP gives none for an LP.

options.text: It raises ValueError, since SCIP returns no dual solution for an LP
options.says: Right: has_dual_feasible_solution() is False for SCIP's LP result, so dual_values raises. Use GLOP or HiGHS for LP prices.

options.text: It never gets there, since SCIP refuses a model with no integer variables
options.says: SCIP solved the LP relaxation to OPTIMAL in the lesson; only GLOP and PDLP refuse a model, and for the opposite reason.

origin.section: Each Solver Accepts Only the Model Types It Can Solve, and Says So Before Solving
